description:
This ticket stands up runtime-demand facts behind the existing seal barrier without moving authority away from the monolith yet. It is a restart from the shadow spike learning, not a cleanup pass over monolith-shaped code.

The fear is not that the fact path prints the same internal trace as `settle_runtime_demands`; the fear is that we accidentally rebuild the monolith in agenda clothing: whole-root maps, global scans, cloned inventories, weakened invariants, and helper signatures that force one-executable work through all-executable data structures.

## Goal
Stand up the first correct-by-construction fact shape for runtime demand:

- `ReturnDemand(E)` is a contribution-joined fact: entry needs, caller observed return use, and callable-boundary return evidence all join into the callee result demand.
- `RuntimeDemand(E)` is the derived executable demand fact: return demand, input demands, value demands, entry-capture demands, call-arg demands, and callable flows for one executable.
- `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)` is an agenda job whose dependencies are explicit facts. The agenda, not a whole-closure inner loop, becomes the fixpoint driver.
- The fact-engine runtime-demand implementation lives in its own module/home. Do not grow the new model inside the monolith-oriented `semantic.rs` surface.

## What We Learned
The original proposal is right for direct calls: `RuntimeDemand(E)` can be derived from facts for `E`, `ReturnDemand(E)`, and the specific `RuntimeDemand(callee)` facts for E local call targets. Self-recursion is still local: when `E` reads its own previous runtime-demand fact, the fresh `ReturnDemand(E)` must win for this firing.

The failed shape was architectural, not cosmetic. Working in the same semantic module encouraged reuse of monolith-shaped helpers whose signatures speak in whole-root `HashMap<ExecutableKey, ...>` terms. That pushed the fact path toward one-element maps, root-wide sets, repeated clone/sort/dedup cycles, and weakened shared invariants so the new path could fit old helper shapes.

Captured local callables need an explicit reverse/indexed relation. The old monolith hides this as a full scan over `all_demands`; the fact path must model it as data keyed by producer identity and capture prefix/surface. Do not recreate the monolith with `RuntimeDemandInventory(root)`, `runtime_demand_keys()`, or any other global scan of all runtime-demand facts.

Equivalence does not mean byte-identical internal maps. The cutover proof is transport projection equivalence. Internal demand provenance and storage shape may differ when the observable transport demand is the same.

## Strategy
Build the new runtime-demand fact engine in a separate module boundary, then connect it to `World`/jobs through narrow facts and effects.

Use monolith code only when the abstraction is neutral. If a helper requires whole-closure maps, global executable sets, or relaxed invariants to serve one executable, do not reuse it. Write a fact-engine-native transfer helper instead.

Prefer data models that make the desired computation natural:

- single-executable `ExecutableFacts`, not one-element `HashMap`s;
- cached lowered-body facts/indexes for producers, delivered joins, dispatch inputs, callsite needs, and local call targets;
- indexed/canonical local callable resolutions, not cloned `Vec`s plus repeated sort/dedup;
- contribution stores with explicit semantics, not copy-pasted activation-input mechanics where publisher replacement and monotone widening mean different things.

## Change
1. Add `FactKey::ReturnDemand(ExecutableKey)` as a cumulative/contribution-joined fact beside `ReturnType` and `ActivationInputs`.
2. Add `FactKey::RuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` as an overwrite fact backed by a runtime-demand store.
3. Add `Job::DeriveRuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` and dispatch. It may read only the facts needed for that executable transfer: executable presence, settled activation/body/callsite facts, `ReturnDemand(E)`, specific neighbor runtime-demand facts, and explicit captured-callable back-link facts introduced by this ticket.
4. Re-express `base_return_demand` as contributions: the root seed contributes entry need, callers contribute observed delivered-result use, and callable-boundary evidence contributes boundary return demand. There is no global `locally_called` prepass in the fact path.
5. Add the captured-local-callable back-link/index as a first-class fact or store relation if the transfer needs it. Shape it around the actual queries the fact engine asks, not around the monolith's full scan.
6. Keep the seal in shadow mode: for every discovered executable, enqueue/wait for `RuntimeDemand(E)` and assert the shadow facts are present and structurally well-formed for that executable frontier. The seal still uses monolith runtime demand as the authoritative output.

## Non-Negotiables
- Do not implement the new runtime-demand engine as more monolith-shaped code inside `semantic.rs`.
- No guessed helper paths left behind. If an attempted model does not pass, remove it before trying the next one.
- No one-element plural-map adapters just to call monolith helpers.
- No `RuntimeDemandInventory`, no root-wide runtime-demand key iteration, and no global locally-called reconstruction in the new fact path.
- Do not weaken monolith invariants to accommodate shadow execution. Split strict monolith helpers from fact-engine helpers instead.
- If captured-callable propagation needs a relationship the current facts cannot express, add the relationship as a first-class fact/index or split the ticket with a new blocking ticket. Do not hide it in scans.
- Do not force byte-for-byte equality between the fact path and monolith internal `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` maps. Internal value/call-arg provenance can differ. The later cutover needs equivalence at the transport projection boundary, not trace identity.

## Why
The agenda should compute runtime-demand facts through explicit dependencies. Direct calls already fit that shape. Captured local callables reveal the missing back-link relation; modeling it explicitly is the difference between incrementalizing the compiler and moving the old full pass into a new container.

The module boundary matters. Keeping the new fact engine outside the monolith-oriented semantic module prevents old whole-world data shapes from becoming accidental requirements of the new design.

## Rip Out
Nothing production-facing yet. The monolith remains authoritative until the shadow path is proven at the consumer boundary.

Any temporary scaffolding added while discovering the correct fact shape must either be removed before commit or tracked by a follow-up ticket that explicitly says when and why it goes away.

## Check
The seal waits for one settled `RuntimeDemand(E)` fact per executable in the monolith frontier and verifies those facts are structurally complete for that frontier. Run the focused runtime-demand tests that cover recursion, first-class callables, direct returned callables, transport callable surfaces, and reducer/suspend-continuation capture. Then run the agreed compiler2/fixture corpus. Zero warnings.

This ticket does not prove cutover equivalence. A follow-up must compare the fact path and monolith at the transport projection boundary before authority moves.
title: Runtime demand: stand up DeriveRuntimeDemand(E) facts behind the seal barrier in shadow mode
